title: Englisch 10 Realschule (ZAM Academy)
description: 46 Lektionen mit englischen Materialien, Sprachaufgaben auf zwei Stufen und 92 gezielten Wiederholungsfragen. Gemeinsamer LehrplanPLUS Bayern; natürliche Hörtexte, Gespräche und längere Lektüre ergänzen die App.

atoms.title: A decision with conditions

practice_items.question: A course is useful, but its timetable is unconfirmed. Which conclusion respects that uncertainty?
practice_items.concept: I would accept if the timetable fitted my other duties.

options: I would accept if the timetable fitted my other duties.
I have definitely been promised a suitable timetable.

practice_items.question: What makes a recommendation conditional rather than absolute?
practice_items.concept: It states a choice together with the circumstances that must hold.
practice_items.sample_solution: For example, “I would accept if travel were affordable” recommends an option without pretending that funding is already confirmed.

atoms.title: A claim is not the evidence

practice_items.question: Six volunteers liked an app, with no comparison group. Which report matches the evidence?
practice_items.concept: Six volunteers reported a positive experience.

options: Six volunteers reported a positive experience.
The app has been proved effective for every teenager.

practice_items.question: Why should a small voluntary survey not be reported as proof about everyone?
practice_items.concept: Its selection and size limit how far its results can be generalised.
practice_items.sample_solution: A precise report names who took part and what they actually reported; broader claims need stronger evidence.

atoms.title: Listen for the change, not the first plan

practice_items.question: A speaker says “Not Tuesday: please come on Wednesday instead.” Which note records the final plan?
practice_items.concept: Meeting: Wednesday.

options: Meeting: Wednesday.
Meeting: Tuesday.

practice_items.question: How can you check a changed arrangement in a conversation?
practice_items.concept: Restate the changed detail and ask the speaker to confirm it.
practice_items.sample_solution: For example, “So the meeting is on Wednesday, not Tuesday—is that right?” checks the exact point rather than guessing.

atoms.title: A complaint with a clear request

practice_items.question: Which sentence makes a complaint both specific and constructive?
practice_items.concept: Building work continued until midnight; could you offer a quiet room tonight?

options: Building work continued until midnight; could you offer a quiet room tonight?
Your staff are useless and everything is always awful.

practice_items.question: Which three elements make a written complaint useful to its recipient?
practice_items.concept: An identifiable problem, supporting details and a clear request for a remedy.
practice_items.sample_solution: For example, give the booking reference and relevant dates, describe what differed from the offer, and ask for a practical next step.

atoms.title: Explain the rule to the right person

practice_items.question: A notice allows free entry only after registration. Which mediation preserves the condition?
practice_items.concept: Entry is free, but you need to register first.

options: Entry is free, but you need to register first.
You can always enter without registering.

practice_items.question: How does mediation differ from translating every sentence?
practice_items.concept: It selects and explains the information a particular recipient needs while preserving its meaning and conditions.
practice_items.sample_solution: For example, a visitor needs access rules and relevant times, but not internal accounting details; an unknown service must remain unknown.

atoms.title: Disagree and keep the conversation moving

practice_items.question: A partner worries that an exchange is too expensive. Which reply addresses that concern?
practice_items.concept: I see the cost problem; could we check whether support is available?

options: I see the cost problem; could we check whether support is available?
You clearly do not care about learning languages.

practice_items.question: Why can summarising another speaker’s view improve a disagreement?
practice_items.concept: It checks understanding and makes clear which actual point your response addresses.
practice_items.sample_solution: A summary such as “Your main concern is cost” does not mean agreement; it helps avoid arguing against a position the speaker never took.

atoms.title: English between different first languages

practice_items.question: Two partners understand “next Friday” as different dates. What should they do?
practice_items.concept: Confirm the exact date before agreeing on the deadline.

options: Confirm the exact date before agreeing on the deadline.
Speak louder and assume the date is now clear.

practice_items.question: What is the purpose of clarification in international communication?
practice_items.concept: To establish shared meaning before people act on a message.
practice_items.sample_solution: A request to rephrase or confirm a date checks understanding; it is useful for speakers with any first language.

atoms.title: Follow a product, not a stereotype

practice_items.question: A parcel is “shipped from Malaysia”. What does this statement establish on its own?
practice_items.concept: It names the place from which the parcel is sent.

options: It names the place from which the parcel is sent.
It proves that every component was manufactured there.

practice_items.question: Why must a summary distinguish production from shipment?
practice_items.concept: The place where a product is sent from may differ from where its parts were made.
practice_items.sample_solution: A careful summary names the relevant stages separately and preserves any conditions on delivery.

atoms.title: An enquiry that can be answered

practice_items.question: A group is collecting offers and has not authorised an order. Which sentence states its purpose accurately?
practice_items.concept: We would like information before deciding whether to order.

options: We would like information before deciding whether to order.
We confirm a binding order for immediate delivery.

practice_items.question: What distinguishes an enquiry from an order?
practice_items.concept: An enquiry requests information; an order communicates a decision to buy under stated conditions.
practice_items.sample_solution: An enquiry can ask about price, delivery or conditions while keeping the purchase decision open. An order communicates the buyer’s decision rather than merely collecting information.

atoms.title: A label and the questions behind it

practice_items.question: Why is “A certification label proves that every trade problem is solved” too strong?
practice_items.concept: A label refers to specified standards, not a guarantee that every problem has disappeared.

options: A label refers to specified standards, not a guarantee that every problem has disappeared.
Any label guarantees identical results in every place and product.

practice_items.question: How should you report a certification claim responsibly?
practice_items.concept: State what the relevant standard covers and what evidence applies to the particular product or supplier.
practice_items.sample_solution: Do not turn a defined certification requirement into a promise that every social or environmental problem is solved.

atoms.title: Who agreed to do what?

practice_items.question: A colleague says “I might be able to find a reviewer.” Which note is accurate?
practice_items.concept: Finding a reviewer is possible but not yet confirmed.

options: Finding a reviewer is possible but not yet confirmed.
The reviewer has definitely accepted the task.

practice_items.question: What three details should a confirmed action point in meeting notes normally contain?
practice_items.concept: The task, the person responsible and the agreed deadline.
practice_items.sample_solution: Keep possible contributions and unresolved conditions separate; they are not confirmed action points.

atoms.title: Turn a shared goal into a plan

practice_items.question: Which action point can a team actually check?
practice_items.concept: Kai will send notes from two user tests by Thursday.

options: Kai will send notes from two user tests by Thursday.
We will somehow make everything better soon.

practice_items.question: Why does a project need intermediate deadlines as well as a final date?
practice_items.concept: Later tasks may depend on earlier results being ready in time.
practice_items.sample_solution: For example, a reviewer needs the draft before the final deadline; a plan should allow time for both stages.

atoms.title: Read the conditions behind a water-saving claim

practice_items.question: Water use falls after a tap is changed, but other conditions also change. What is justified?
practice_items.concept: The values fell, but the tap alone has not been proved to cause the change.

options: The values fell, but the tap alone has not been proved to cause the change.
The new tap must cause the same reduction in every home.

practice_items.question: Why should a report separate an observed change from its possible cause?
practice_items.concept: Different conditions may contribute to the change, so a numerical difference alone does not establish causation.
practice_items.sample_solution: For example, lower model water use may occur while both a tap and the number of visitors change. You can calculate the fall, but the comparison does not isolate the tap as its only cause.

atoms.title: Compare energy options by the same measure

practice_items.question: An option produces the most energy but exceeds the stated budget. Which recommendation is careful?
practice_items.concept: It has the highest model output, but affordability must also be considered.

options: It has the highest model output, but affordability must also be considered.
The largest output automatically makes it affordable.

practice_items.question: Why should the criteria of an energy comparison be stated before a recommendation?
practice_items.concept: Different goals and constraints can make different options reasonable.
practice_items.sample_solution: The highest model output alone does not decide affordability, available space or other relevant conditions.

atoms.title: A useful tool still needs a check

practice_items.question: A fluent translation changes “only after registration” into “without registration”. What should happen before publication?
practice_items.concept: A reviewer should check and correct the changed meaning.

options: A reviewer should check and correct the changed meaning.
Fluent wording makes a meaning check unnecessary.

practice_items.question: Why does a fluent technical output still need verification?
practice_items.concept: Fluency does not establish factual accuracy or preserve every condition of the source.
practice_items.sample_solution: Check the relevant meaning, especially dates, negation and conditions, and make clear who is responsible for the final version.

atoms.title: From a local trial to a limited conclusion

practice_items.question: A lunch trial has a different menu and unknown attendance. Which conclusion is justified?
practice_items.concept: The local observation is interesting, but the changed conditions limit the comparison.

options: The local observation is interesting, but the changed conditions limit the comparison.
It proves what every pupil everywhere should eat.

practice_items.question: What should a report do when important comparison details are missing?
practice_items.concept: Identify the missing details and limit its conclusion accordingly.
practice_items.sample_solution: A report can describe a local observation while explaining why a broader recommendation needs a better comparison.

atoms.title: What the chart does—and does not—say

practice_items.question: Twelve of twenty workshop participants choose repair ideas. Which statement stays within the data?
practice_items.concept: Repair ideas received the most choices in this workshop.

options: Repair ideas received the most choices in this workshop.
The result proves that most people in every country prefer repair ideas.

practice_items.question: What is the difference between describing a chart and explaining its causes?
practice_items.concept: Description reports the values; a causal explanation needs additional evidence about why they occurred.
practice_items.sample_solution: A bar showing twelve choices establishes how often an option was selected. It does not establish whether people chose it because of cost, interest or another reason; that needs additional evidence.

atoms.title: Make a case and test the objection

practice_items.question: Which conclusion weighs a benefit and a real constraint?
practice_items.concept: A small trial may be useful if suitable supervision and rules are confirmed.

options: A small trial may be useful if suitable supervision and rules are confirmed.
A useful idea never needs supervision or rules.

practice_items.question: What makes a counterargument useful in an opinion text?
practice_items.concept: It challenges a relevant part of the reasoning and is addressed fairly before the final judgement.
practice_items.sample_solution: A real constraint such as unconfirmed supervision should be weighed, not replaced by a personal attack.

atoms.title: A language is more than a greeting

practice_items.question: You are unsure how to pronounce a host’s name. Which response avoids making an assumption?
practice_items.concept: Could you tell me how you would like me to pronounce your name?

options: Could you tell me how you would like me to pronounce your name?
Your name proves which language you always prefer.

practice_items.question: Why should cultural communication include questions about individual preferences?
practice_items.concept: People within the same country or language community can have different experiences and preferences.
practice_items.sample_solution: Ask the person how they want a name pronounced or a conversation conducted rather than assuming a preference from their background.

atoms.title: A historical date needs a question

practice_items.question: A short source gives a treaty’s signing date. What does that establish by itself?
practice_items.concept: The date of the event described, not a complete account of every participant’s experience.

options: The date of the event described, not a complete account of every participant’s experience.
That every participant had an identical view of everything that followed.

practice_items.question: Why is a source’s perspective relevant when reading history in English?
practice_items.concept: It helps identify whose experiences and purposes are represented and what may be missing.
practice_items.sample_solution: A source can provide reliable event details without containing every participant’s interpretation; compare perspectives before making a broad claim.

atoms.title: Two voices are not a national character

practice_items.question: Two writers prefer different meeting routines because their travel situations differ. Which comparison is supported?
practice_items.concept: Both value contact, but their travel situations shape different preferences.

options: Both value contact, but their travel situations shape different preferences.
Their country makes every person prefer exactly the same routine.

practice_items.question: How can you compare cultural perspectives without stereotyping?
practice_items.concept: Compare specific evidence from the people or texts and avoid extending it automatically to a whole group.
practice_items.sample_solution: For example, both writers may value contact while different travel needs shape their preferred meeting format. Compare those stated situations rather than treating either voice as the view of a whole country.

atoms.title: A visitor needs the condition, too

practice_items.question: A notice says “Guests may join if places are available.” Which German mediation preserves the meaning?
practice_items.concept: Gäste können teilnehmen, wenn Plätze frei sind.

options: Gäste können teilnehmen, wenn Plätze frei sind.
Für jeden Gast ist bereits ein Platz garantiert.

practice_items.question: Why must mediation distinguish missing information from a prohibition?
practice_items.concept: A text that does not mention a service has not necessarily forbidden it.
practice_items.sample_solution: Report the information gap and ask the organiser; do not invent either a guarantee or a ban.

atoms.title: More than one public language

practice_items.question: Which language gained official status in South Africa in 2023?
practice_items.concept: South African Sign Language.

options: South African Sign Language.
English.

practice_items.question: Why does a country’s official-language list not determine every individual’s preferred language?
practice_items.concept: Legal or public status and a person’s language experience or preference are different things.
practice_items.sample_solution: Use the country information as context, then ask the person what will make the specific communication clear and accessible.

atoms.title: A political turning point and its limits

practice_items.question: Which year marks South Africa’s first democratic election?
Why is “a political turning point” different from “the end of every social problem”?
practice_items.concept: A political event can change institutions without proving that every social inequality has immediately disappeared.
practice_items.sample_solution: A careful historical account identifies the event and then investigates longer-term developments with appropriate evidence.

atoms.title: Hear support and concern in the same voice

practice_items.question: A speaker says “I welcome the idea, but the finishing time is a problem.” What is her position?
practice_items.concept: She supports the goal but questions a practical arrangement.

options: She supports the goal but questions a practical arrangement.
She rejects every part of the idea.

practice_items.question: How can you identify a speaker’s attitude when a statement contains “but”?
practice_items.concept: Check which part expresses support and which part introduces a concern or limit.
practice_items.sample_solution: A concern about timing may qualify support for an activity rather than reject the activity itself.

atoms.title: Report a voice without changing its reach

practice_items.question: A writer says “English helps me talk to visitors in this club.” Which paraphrase preserves the scope?
practice_items.concept: The writer finds English useful for speaking to visitors in the club.

options: The writer finds English useful for speaking to visitors in the club.
The writer says everyone must use only English in every situation.

practice_items.question: Which details must a fair paraphrase preserve even when its wording changes?
practice_items.concept: The source, the central meaning and relevant limits such as purpose, frequency or conditions.
practice_items.sample_solution: Replacing “sometimes, for this project” with “always, for everyone” changes the claim instead of merely rewording it.

atoms.title: Choose the time relationship

practice_items.question: You name a finished event at a specified past time: “We ___ the draft yesterday.” Which form fits?
practice_items.concept: finished

options: finished
have finished

practice_items.question: How does “was checking when the phone rang” organise the two actions?
practice_items.concept: It presents checking as the ongoing background and the phone call as an event that occurred during it.
practice_items.sample_solution: The past continuous and simple past show the relationship between a continuing activity and a shorter event.

atoms.title: Permission is not obligation

practice_items.question: What does “You do not have to bring a laptop” mean?
practice_items.concept: Bringing a laptop is not required.

options: Bringing a laptop is not required.
Bringing a laptop is forbidden.

practice_items.question: How do “do not have to” and “must not” differ?
practice_items.concept: Do not have to means there is no obligation; must not expresses a prohibition.
practice_items.sample_solution: An optional item is not automatically forbidden. Use the form that matches the actual rule.

atoms.title: Guessing about the past

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an Permission is not obligation an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.
Die Lektion knüpft an Choose the time relationship an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: Which sentence explicitly presents a possible past explanation rather than a confirmed fact?
practice_items.concept: The key might have fallen out of my pocket.

options: The key might have fallen out of my pocket.
The key definitely fell out of my pocket.

practice_items.question: What does “might have happened” communicate?
practice_items.concept: A possibility concerning a past event, not a confirmed fact.
practice_items.sample_solution: The structure is might + have + past participle. Its uncertainty must be preserved when the claim is reported again.

atoms.title: Advice after the event

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an Permission is not obligation an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: After missing a deadline, which sentence gives retrospective advice?
practice_items.concept: I should have checked the date earlier.

options: I should have checked the date earlier.
I should check the date tomorrow.

practice_items.question: In a reflection on a missed deadline, what does “I should have checked it” express?
practice_items.concept: A retrospective judgement that checking would have been the better past action.
practice_items.sample_solution: It differs from “I should check it now,” which advises an action in the present or future.

atoms.title: Possible or conditional?

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an Guessing about the past an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.
Die Lektion knüpft an Advice after the event an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: A speaker says that, if informed, they would definitely have chosen to attend. Which sentence expresses that conditional result?
practice_items.concept: I would have joined if I had known about it.

options: I would have joined if I had known about it.
I might have joined, but I am not saying what I would have chosen.

practice_items.question: Why can “could have” not always be read as a definitely unused opportunity?
practice_items.concept: In some contexts it expresses a possible explanation of a past event whose truth is unknown.
practice_items.sample_solution: “It could have been moved; we do not know” is a deduction, while “I could have joined, but chose not to” explicitly states an unused opportunity.

atoms.title: A sound, a noun and a context

practice_items.question: Which sentence uses the uncountable noun advice correctly?
practice_items.concept: The tutor gave me some advice.

options: The tutor gave me some advice.
The tutor gave me an advice.

practice_items.question: What determines the choice between a and an?
practice_items.concept: The initial sound of the following word, not simply its first written letter.
practice_items.sample_solution: For example, an hour begins with a vowel sound, whereas a university begins with a consonant sound.

atoms.title: A pair is not always two subjects

practice_items.question: Which sentence treats one pair as the subject?
practice_items.concept: A pair of scissors is missing.

options: A pair of scissors is missing.
A pair of scissors are missing because scissors is the nearest noun.

practice_items.question: Why is the verb singular in “A pair of scissors is missing”?
practice_items.concept: The grammatical head is the singular noun pair.
practice_items.sample_solution: The plural noun inside of scissors does not change the singular head; compare “Two pairs of scissors are missing.”

atoms.title: The condition hidden in unless

practice_items.question: What does “We will meet outside unless it rains” mean in this plan?
practice_items.concept: We will meet outside if it does not rain.

options: We will meet outside if it does not rain.
We will meet outside only if it rains.

practice_items.question: How can you check whether an unless-sentence expresses the intended condition?
practice_items.concept: Test what the main action means when the exception is true and when it is not.
practice_items.sample_solution: “Meet outside unless it rains” gives rain as the exception; in this context it means “meet outside if it does not rain.”

atoms.title: Build a word, then check its role

practice_items.question: Which word is a noun in “We discussed the usefulness of the example”?
practice_items.concept: usefulness

options: usefulness
useful

practice_items.question: Why should word formation be checked against sentence context?
practice_items.concept: A familiar stem or ending is only a clue; the required word class and actual meaning depend on usage.
practice_items.sample_solution: Compare useful as an adjective with usefulness as a noun, then verify an unfamiliar form with context and a dictionary.

atoms.title: The particle changes the job

practice_items.question: Which version uses the pronoun correctly with put off in the meaning postpone?
practice_items.concept: We can put it off.

options: We can put it off.
We can put off it.

practice_items.question: Why should a phrasal verb be learned with an example sentence as well as a translation?
practice_items.concept: The example shows its meaning in context and how its object is positioned.
practice_items.sample_solution: Compare separable put it off with look after her; the same word-order rule does not apply to every multi-word verb.

atoms.title: Words that work together

practice_items.question: Which common collocation fits an ordinary project report?
practice_items.concept: We made a decision after doing research.

options: We made a decision after doing research.
We did a decision after making research.

practice_items.question: What is the benefit of learning a collocation rather than isolated translated words?
practice_items.concept: It records a common combination that helps express the intended meaning naturally.
practice_items.sample_solution: For example, learn make a decision and do research as chunks instead of assuming that the same verb works with both nouns.

atoms.title: To does not always introduce an infinitive

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an Build a word, then check its role an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: Which sentence uses look forward to with the correct following verb form?
practice_items.concept: We look forward to meeting you.

options: We look forward to meeting you.
We look forward to meet you.

practice_items.question: Why does “look forward to meeting” use an ing-form although it contains to?
practice_items.concept: To is a preposition within look forward to, not the infinitive marker in that expression.
practice_items.sample_solution: Compare look forward to meeting you with want to meet you; the full pattern determines the following form.

atoms.title: The Spare Chair

practice_items.question: In a first-person story, the narrator reports “Sam looked at the chair” but gives no access to Sam’s thoughts. What can a reader claim directly?
practice_items.concept: Sam’s action is reported; his exact thought is not directly stated.

options: Sam’s action is reported; his exact thought is not directly stated.
The narrator knows and states every thought Sam has.

practice_items.question: How does a literary interpretation differ from a direct statement of the plot?
practice_items.concept: It explains a possible meaning of text details and supports that reading with evidence.
practice_items.sample_solution: A reader may connect repeated objects and changes in behaviour, while distinguishing the text’s observations from inferred motives.

atoms.title: Mansfield: light and a faint chill

practice_items.question: An opening contrasts “the blue sky powdered with gold” with “a faint chill”. What does the contrast show?
practice_items.concept: A bright visual impression can coexist with a feeling of cold.

options: A bright visual impression can coexist with a feeling of cold.
Bright imagery proves that no character can feel any cold.

practice_items.question: What should happen before a claim about an entire literary work is based on its opening paragraph?
practice_items.concept: The reader should check the claim against further relevant passages of the work.
practice_items.sample_solution: A close reading of the opening gives a starting point; later evidence may confirm, complicate or change the first interpretation.

atoms.title: A review gives reasons, not only stars

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an The Spare Chair an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: Which review sentence supports a judgement with a text detail?
practice_items.concept: The repeated chair makes the quiet change at the end meaningful.

options: The repeated chair makes the quiet change at the end meaningful.
The story is good because it is good.

practice_items.question: What turns a review’s opinion into a reasoned evaluation?
practice_items.concept: A clear judgement linked to relevant evidence and a stated criterion or reader need.
practice_items.sample_solution: “I recommend it because the repeated object creates a meaningful ending” gives more than an unexplained positive label.

atoms.title: What changes when a story becomes an image?

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an The Spare Chair an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: A storyboard shows a face but gives no spoken or written inner thought. What can an analysis claim directly?
practice_items.concept: It can describe the visible image and discuss a possible interpretation.

options: It can describe the visible image and discuss a possible interpretation.
It proves every exact thought of the character.

practice_items.question: Why must a media comparison distinguish a storyboard from a finished film?
practice_items.concept: A storyboard is a plan and does not establish the actual movement, sound or final effects of a completed film.
practice_items.sample_solution: Describe what a storyboard proposes, then use a genuinely viewed completed work to discuss its realised effects. A plan alone cannot show the final pacing, performed movement, sound or editing.

atoms.title: Present a choice, then answer the question

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an What the chart does—and does not—say an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: A listener asks for a cost that your source does not give. Which response is responsible?
practice_items.concept: The model does not include that cost; I would need another source to answer.

options: The model does not include that cost; I would need another source to answer.
I will invent a precise figure so that the answer sounds confident.

practice_items.question: What should determine the selection of language and supporting media in a presentation?
practice_items.concept: Its purpose, the audience’s prior knowledge and the evidence needed for the main points.
practice_items.sample_solution: Choose a graphic that supports the explanation, define unfamiliar terms and keep source limits visible during questions.

atoms.title: Meaning, stress and a useful pause

practice_items.question: In the usual pronunciation contrast, where is the main stress in the verb record?
practice_items.concept: On the second syllable.

options: On the second syllable.
On the first syllable, exactly as in the noun.

practice_items.question: Why should pronunciation be checked in the dictionary entry for the word’s actual use?
practice_items.concept: The same spelling can have different meanings, word classes or stress patterns.
practice_items.sample_solution: For example, the usual noun/verb stress contrast in record is clearer when each form is learned in its own sentence.

atoms.title: Revise one problem at a time

practice_items.question: Which feedback gives a concrete, usable revision target?
practice_items.concept: The second sentence contradicts the registration rule; keep that condition.

options: The second sentence contradicts the registration rule; keep that condition.
The whole text is simply bad.

practice_items.question: What makes feedback actionable?
practice_items.concept: It identifies a specific feature or passage, explains the issue and points towards a relevant improvement.
practice_items.sample_solution: A learner can then revise that part and assess the change, instead of reacting to an unexplained label such as good or bad.

atoms.title: Investigate a question that matters now

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an Revise one problem at a time an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: A project template has headings but no sources have been read. What can honestly be claimed?
practice_items.concept: The plan is prepared, but the research has not yet been completed.

options: The plan is prepared, but the research has not yet been completed.
The template proves that all current findings have already been checked.

practice_items.question: Why should a research report distinguish a plan from checked findings?
practice_items.concept: A plan describes intended work; findings require sources that were actually read and evaluated.
practice_items.sample_solution: Report completed evidence honestly, keep unfinished steps visible and never invent quotations or results to fill a template.
